scholarships.title: NTNU PhD Positions (Salaried Employment)
scholarships.funding_label: Fully Funded (salaried employment as a PhD research fellow / stipendiat)
scholarships.official_source: Norwegian University of Science and Technology (NTNU)

existing.description: NTNU's PhD positions are salaried employment rather than scholarships: Norwegian PhD candidates are not treated as students and are normally employees of the institution that funds them. Most PhD candidates at NTNU are employed as PhD research fellows (stipendiat) at NTNU or a university college, with individual positions advertised on NTNU's vacancy pages and on jobbnorge.no. Admission requires at least five years of higher education including a master's degree, a weighted average of at least B over the last two master's years on NTNU's scale, and a funding plan for the whole PhD period. Acceptance is done continuously throughout the academic year rather than at fixed deadlines, and the standard PhD is three years full-time, sometimes extended by a fourth year of teaching duties.
eligibility: At least five years of higher education including a master's degree or other equivalent degree
A strong academic record: weighted average for the last two years of the master's degree equivalent to a B or higher in NTNU's grading scale
A funding plan covering the entire PhD period - financing is an absolute requirement for acceptance
At least two academic supervisors, at least one of whom (usually the main supervisor) must be employed at NTNU, including for externally funded candidates
Foreign education may need NOKUT recognition or a faculty-level assessment
Individual faculties or programmes may set further qualification requirements
existing.eligibility_summary: Five years of higher education including a master's degree or equivalent, a strong academic record with a weighted average for the last two years of the master's degree equivalent to a B or higher on NTNU's grading scale, and a confirmed funding plan for the whole PhD period.
benefits: Salaried employment as a PhD research fellow (stipendiat) at NTNU or a university college
Norwegian public-sector pension and employee benefit schemes
Access to NTNU International Researcher Support (NIRS) for administrative and relocation help
coverage: Salary as an NTNU employee (PhD research fellow / stipendiat) under the Norwegian state pay scale
Pension and employee benefit schemes through employment
No separate tuition, travel or accommodation funding is published on these pages
requirements: Secure a funding plan for the whole PhD period before acceptance
Contact the research group and identify a potential main supervisor early, with at least two academic supervisors in total
Prepare the application in cooperation with the main supervisor
Submit through the department to the faculty, using the faculty's or programme's own form where one exists
For positions in the final year of high school-equivalent entry, individual vacancy advertisements state the full requirement list
documents: Documentation of former education qualifying you for a PhD, with diploma supplement and/or NOKUT assessment if available
Documentation of education obtained outside of Norway
Documentation of funding for the entire PhD period
Project description, complete or preliminary (a complete version within six months of admission if a preliminary one is accepted)
Details of legal or ethical issues related to the project, plus ethics committee or other approval where required
The fixed NTNU PhD application form
application_method: Apply to an individually advertised PhD vacancy. The application is written in cooperation with the main supervisor and sent to the faculty through the department. Positions are announced on NTNU's web pages and on jobbnorge.no.
existing.selection_notes: Assessment is continuous through the academic year and is not restricted to the start of a term. NTNU requires a strong academic record and a confirmed funding plan; at least one supervisor must be employed at NTNU.
existing.best_fit: Research-oriented PhD candidates seeking salaried positions at NTNU
existing.duration: Three-year full-time study as standard; some positions include a fourth year of required duties, usually teaching, as detailed in the employee contract
existing.application_period: Continuous - individual PhD vacancies are posted on NTNU's vacancy pages and on jobbnorge.no and are assessed as they arrive.
existing.deadline_display: Positions are advertised individually and applications are assessed continuously: 'Acceptance to a PhD-programme at NTNU is done continuously throughout the academic year and is not restricted to the beginning of term.' Each vacancy carries its own application deadline.
